s: A solutions architect at a large company needs to set up network security tor outbound traffic to the internet from all AWS accounts within an organization in AWS Organizations. The organization has more than 100 AWS accounts, and the accounts route to each other by using a centralized AWS Transit Gateway. Each account has both an internet gateway and a NAT gateway tor outbound traffic to the internet The company deploys resources only into a single AWS Region. The company needs the ability to add centrally managed rule-based filtering on all outbound traffic to the internet for all AWS accounts in the organization. The peak load of outbound traffic will not exceed 25 Gbps in each Availability Zone. Which solution meets these requirements?
o: Create a new VPC for outbound traffic to the internet. Connect the existing transit gateway to the new VPC. Configure a new NAT gateway. Create an Auto Scaling group of Amazon EC2 instances that run an open-source internet proxy for rule-based filtering across all Availability Zones in the Region. Modify all default routes to point to the proxy's Auto Scaling group.

Create a new VPC for outbound traffic to the internet. Connect the existing transit gateway to the new VPC. Configure a new NAT gateway. Use an AWS Network Firewall firewall for rule-based filtering. Create Network Firewall endpoints in each Availability Zone. Modify all default routes to point to the Network Firewall endpoints.
Create an AWS Network Firewall firewall for rule-based filtering in each AWS account. Modify all default routes to point to the Network Firewall firewalls in each account.

In each AWS account, create an Auto Scaling group of network-optimized Amazon EC2 instances that run an open-source internet proxy for rule-based filtering. Modify all default routes to point to the proxy's Auto Scaling group.

w.y: The filtering must be centrally managed across more than 100 accounts that already share a transit gateway. A centralized egress VPC attached to the transit gateway, with AWS Network Firewall endpoints in each AZ in front of a NAT gateway, inspects all outbound traffic in one place. Network Firewall is managed and each endpoint scales well beyond 25 Gbps per AZ.

o.A: A self-managed proxy fleet means patching, scaling and HA work, and default routes can't point at an Auto Scaling group.
o.B: Correct: a centralized egress VPC with Network Firewall endpoints per AZ behind the transit gateway gives managed, scalable, central filtering.
o.C: A firewall in every account is costly and not centrally managed (it would need Firewall Manager, which isn't mentioned).
o.D: Per-account proxy fleets are decentralized, costly and heavy to operate.
